key_insight: An explicit block-encoding of the shifted finite element stiffness matrix enables a resource-efficient quantum framework for 2D isotropic linear elasticity.
engineering_relevance: The framework identifies conditions for polynomial quantum speedups in displacement state preparation, strain energy estimation, and low-resolution displacement reconstruction.
method: Analytically diagonalize element stiffness matrices and factorize global finite element assembly.
Construct normalized block-encoding with constant ancilla count and gate complexity logarithmic in the number of degrees of freedom.
Use quantum singular value transformation for linear-system solving with improved condition-number dependence.
evidence_signal: Numerical cantilever beam experiments verify the proposed circuits and show agreement with conventional finite element solutions.
watch_item: Speedups are conditional; efficient block-encoding alone does not establish end-to-end advantage for loading inputs or reconstructing full displacement fields.
paper_title: Quantum algorithmic framework for finite element analysis of isotropic linear elastic materials via efficient block-encoding
